rootCause: The cause is uninitialized state in every Sound. The LFO class (lfo.h:35-37, `LFO() = default`) leaves phase and holdValue unset; this affects Sound::globalLFO and ModControllableAudio::modFXLFO. Sound::Sound() only sets `skippingRendering = true` (sound.cpp:150), without startSkippingRendering(). So the three timestamps timeStartedSkippingRendering{ModFX,LFO,Arp} (sound.h:153-155) stay unset. The first note calls stopSkippingRendering() (sound.cpp:2522-2534, Arp 2563). There the LFO is advanced by audioSampleTimer minus the old value, the mod FX LFO by modFXTimeOff, and gatePos is shifted accordingly. A free-running LFO1 never gets a start phase, because resyncGlobalLFO() only sets the phase with sync. This is how the layout dependence arises: in the first loaded Sound, timeStartedSkippingRenderingLFO holds a stale pointer into .rodata (0x201c77bc in v12, 0x201cbd48 in the control build).
uninitialisedReads: The following is proven. With RAM fills of 0xA5 and 0x5A before the boot, the outputs differ from window 1 on. For this, .bss is cleared as in initsct (the harness skips initsct). If the five fields are zeroed after loading, the outputs are identical over 400 windows. To narrow it down, both the timestamps and the LFO phases were needed. A remainder is left: from bar 2 on, 71 samples differ by ±1 LSB. The source lies in small heap blocks of the loading process at 0x202f29xx-2fxx: FFT configurations 8/16, the wavetable band array and a patch cable array. The exact read location is not determined. The remainder is 0 in both builds and therefore not layout-dependent. Found on the side: the arpeggiator field whichNoteCurrentlyOnPostArp is read without initialization. The memory hooks of unicorn 2.1.4 distort the emulation, so the search was done differentially with RAM dumps and zeroing.
audibleOnDevice: Yes, audible on the device. It is not a deviation in the last bit: between the two layouts the RMS difference is −25 dB relative to the signal, at most 1444 LSB. LFO1 and the chorus, phaser and flanger LFOs start with a random phase, depending on the previous RAM content. The same song file therefore sounds modulated differently on every load, e.g. the filter movement is at a different point. With S&H or random-walk LFOs, holdValue is garbage. Random walk can therefore start with an extreme offset that decays only slowly. For the arp, gatePos of the first note after loading is shifted.
fixProposal: First, set default initializers in lfo.h: `uint32_t phase = 0; int32_t holdValue = 0;`. Second, in the constructor Sound::Sound() set the three timeStartedSkippingRendering* fields to AudioEngine::audioSampleTimer, as startSkippingRendering() does, but without stopParamLPF. In addition, for cleanliness, initialize globalSourceValues{} and, in the arpeggiator, whichNoteCurrentlyOnPostArp, gatePos and currentOctave/Direction. The unused field numSamplesSkippedRenderingForGlobalLFO can be removed. Not implemented.
comparisonRecipe: Run `EMU_OPTS="--init-sounds --seed 1" ./run.sh <tree|elf> <out>` for both ELFs, then compare the `sha256sum` of the two demand-measured.wav. `--init-sounds` intercepts Sound::Sound() and sets the five fields the way the fix would; the offsets come from DWARF via gdb. `--seed` fixes jcong after the boot, because the seed comes from TCNT_0 and so depends on the instruction count. `--fill WORD` checks whether uninitialized RAM is read. All options are documented in the header of run.sh and implemented in song_emu.py (/home/user/deluge/mastertune-1.2.1/tests/song/).
evidence: Without options v12 still gives b6766a67. With `--init-sounds --seed 1`, v12 and filters-ctl give an identical 004893b8 (1 lead-in bar, 4 bars). With `--init-sounds` alone both are also identical (ae0d4e6e). jcong after the boot is the same in both builds (0xabf95468), so the seed is not the cause. The results are in /home/user/work/layout-rc.

reproduced:
For an independent test I made my own build: /home/user/work/layout-chk, v12 f89b478c, which differs from v12 only in RELEASE_TYPE (mastertune-v12-layoutcheck-q). This shifts .rodata by 16 bytes. In the other agent's filters-ctl build, padding and RELEASE_TYPE were mixed; here it is only the version string.
- The demand run without options gives 7570050f. That is neither b6766a67 nor aa3cec96, so the build is layout-dependent, as expected.
- With `--init-sounds --seed 1` it gives 004893b8. That is bit-identical to v12 and filters-ctl. jcong is identical in all builds (0xabf95468).
- I recalculated the numbers from the existing WAVs: v12 against ctl without options is at −25.6 dB RMS and at most 1444 LSB, which is correct.
- I checked the code. lfo.h:35-37, sound.cpp:150 (only skippingRendering = true) and stopSkippingRendering (2522-2534, Arp 2563) are correct. resyncGlobalLFO() aborts without a running clock and only sets the phase with sync.
problems:
1. The claim about audibility is overstated. The −25 dB only compare two arbitrary phases in the emulator. On the device, the start phase of a free-running LFO1 or mod FX LFO depends anyway on the wait between loading and play. This also holds with the fix, which advances the tick by timer minus construction time. What is really audible is mainly the random-walk LFO: if holdValue is garbage, it starts with an offset of up to about ten times the range, which decays by only 1/16 per period. With S&H, garbage only affects the first period; the arp gatePos offset is marginal.
2. The fix proposal is partly redundant. gatePos and currentOctave already have initializers (arpeggiator.h:271, 313). Only whichNoteCurrentlyOnPostArp (h:312) is missing.
3. The recipe is song-specific. `--init-sounds` only intercepts Sound::Sound(). It does not cover modFXLFO in other ModControllableAudio objects, i.e. audio clips and the song's GlobalEffectable. The lfo.h fix would cover these too. For the test song this does not matter, for songs with mod FX on audio tracks it does.
4. A dependence on never-written heap remains (±1 LSB, 71 samples). The recipe is only bit-exact as long as fresh heap is zero, as in the emulator.
So the finding on the cause and the recipe hold for this song.
